liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (1 review): Contains some really great guitar moments from Jerry [19]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Brent takes two choruses, perhaps another, before Jerry's solo [19]
- **My Brother Esau** (1 review): Esau has a few lyrics that differ from usual [9]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): The Lost Sailor into Saint of Circumstance sequence is full of energy [8]

## The recordings

- **gd1983-03-31.sbd.miller.32306.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 145 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1983-03-31.mtx.seamons.94016.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 21 songs; 143 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [2]
- **gd1983-03-31.sbd.miller.77086.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 146 min; rated 3.5/5 by 12 [3]. Said about its sound: Soundboard mix is good, though vocals and Brent's keyboards sit too loud; Soundboard sounds like the band is playing in your living room; Brent's B3 seems to be run through a different amp than his usual 122s [12][13][16][17][19]
- **gd1983-03-31.sbd.unknown.32296.flac16**: soundboard; 21 songs; 146 min [4]. Said about its sound: Quality is good given the generations; there are small cuts in Drums and Space from the tape flip [4]
- **gd83-03-31.aud.miller.18112.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 21 songs; 141 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [5]
- **gd1983-03-31.162264.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 21 songs; 146 min [6]

## Around the show

- Tickets were easy to get and the crowd was great [8]
- Reviewer says it was the smallest venue they ever attended for the band [14]
- This Terrapin and The Other One resemble the Binghampton versions; show fits the solid Spring '83 tour [8]
- The mix is better than that of earlier Warfield shows [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1983-03-31.sbd.miller.32306.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette [1]
- **gd1983-03-31.mtx.seamons.94016.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: Soundboard went to Dolby B cassette master, then Nakamichi DR-1, Sony R500 and Samplitude, ending as FLAC, all by Charlie Miller; Audience source used Sennheiser 421 mics into Sony D5, then DAT, transferred by Charlie Miller; Hunter Seamons made a matrix of the soundboard and audience using Final Cut Pro [2]
- **gd1983-03-31.sbd.miller.77086.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette (Dolby B) [3]
- **gd1983-03-31.sbd.unknown.32296.flac16**: source: SBD > C(x5) > Sony TC-D5M > Soundblaster > WAV > Soundforge > CD-Wave > TLH v.1.0.0.72 (SBE-OK, checksums, Flac compression) > bt.etree 01/06. [4]. Also: Cassettes were labeled fifth-generation soundboard, which the sound supports; A slightly degraded soundboard source covers the tuning track and part of Drums through The Other One [4]
- **gd83-03-31.aud.miller.18112.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sennheiser 421 -> Cm (Sony D5) -> Dat via Charlie Miller [5]
- **gd1983-03-31.162264.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (TDK MA-R90) [6]. Also: A short soundboard patch of about 54 seconds fills part of Drums [6]
